title: APIM AI Gateway: Content Safety for Streaming Responses
summary: A hands-on guide to llm-content-safety, managed identity, regex blocklists, eight policy scenarios, current debug tracing, and the detection-versus-latency tradeoffs of streaming windows and overlap.
sourceDocuments: APIM AI Gateway: llm-content-safety Outbound Streaming Inspection Lab Guide

downloads.label: Passthrough baseline policy (XML)
downloads.description: Byte-identical reviewed source companion. Routes and authenticates model requests with streaming passthrough; it does not enable Content Safety inspection.

downloads.label: Passthrough baseline ARM payload (JSON)
downloads.description: Byte-identical reviewed source companion whose rawxml value equals base-policy.xml. It does not enable Content Safety inspection.

downloads.label: Source-derived outbound categories and blocklist policy (XML)
downloads.description: Complete API-level example combining the source baseline with outbound inspection at window 3000/overlap 500 and the synthetic lab blocklist pii-known-values. Requires provisioning, RBAC, manual backend managed-identity configuration, and blocklist registration; not deployed or Azure-validated in this editorial review.

omissions: The original-language source, private repository location, commit metadata, local paths, and environment identifiers are withheld; this article and its samples contain English descriptions and neutral lab variables only.

Original request and response bodies, analyzedChunk values, full traces, credentials, resource endpoints, subscription, tenant, principal, and blocklist item identifiers are not published. Identifier-shaped examples are deliberately invalid synthetic format fixtures.

Historical observations are retained but were not re-run during this editorial review. No raw benchmark dataset, deterministic replay backend, production test harness, or measured latency distribution is supplied by the source.

The source does not establish exact Content Safety call counts, universal first-flush timing, Unicode window counting semantics, a complete messages/tools serialization model, or a universal inbound cutoff from JSON byte size.
No verified backend credentials.managedIdentity REST contract is claimed for the reviewed ARM API versions. The required portal managed-identity configuration remains a manual step.

Retired master-subscription tracing and SAS trace-download procedures are not reproduced as executable instructions. Use short-lived API-specific debug credentials and authenticated listTrace instead.
